Title: Proteogenomic and metabolomic characterization of human glioblastoma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary glioblastoma tumor tissue; normal brain tissue (GTEx)
Disease Subtype: Untreated glioblastoma with and without isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 and 2 mutations.
Experimental Design: CPTAC glioblastoma discovery study using TMT11-based global proteome, phosphoproteome, and acetylome profiling of treatment-naïve primary GBM tissues and GTEx normal brain controls. Samples were analyzed by multidimensional LC-MS/MS with bRPLC fractionation and Orbitrap-based DDA acquisition. Integrated multi-omics analysis included whole-genome/exome sequencing, RNA-seq, single-nucleus RNA-seq, DNA methylation, lipidomics, and metabolomics to characterize signaling pathways, immune microenvironment, metabolic reprogramming, and subtype-specific molecular features in glioblastoma.
Short Description: Comprehensive CPTAC proteogenomic and metabolomic characterization of human glioblastoma integrating proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome, genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics from treatment-naïve GBM tumors and normal brain tissues. The study identified immune-associated and metabolic GBM subtypes, subtype-specific kinase signaling networks, lipid remodeling patterns, and proteome-level heterogeneity not fully explained by genomic alterations alone.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic and metabolomic profiling identified molecular subtypes of glioblastoma associated with survival, immune microenvironment remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and distinct signaling pathway activation patterns.
Data_Caveats: Normal brain controls were partially derived from Genotype-Tissue Expression Project datasets rather than fully matched adjacent tissues, introducing potential batch effects and differences in sample procurement, processing, and donor composition relative to glioblastoma specimens.

Title: The AML Microenvironment Catalyzes a Step-wise Evolution to Gilteritinib Resistance
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia cell lines MOLM14 and MV411 with parental state, early gilteritinib-resistant state under fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand stimulation, and late gilteritinib-resistant state
Disease Subtype: FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia with stepwise acquisition of resistance to gilteritinib mediated by bone marrow microenvironment signaling
Experimental Design: TMT11-based proteome and phosphoproteome profiling of FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia cell lines MOLM14 and MV411 during stepwise development of resistance to gilteritinib. The dataset includes parental control states, early resistant states induced by fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand stimulation, and late resistant states with stable autonomous resistance.
Short Description: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic characterization of early microenvironment-dependent and late autonomous resistance to gilteritinib in FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia cell line models.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of MOLM14 and MV411 acute myeloid leukemia cell lines identified distinct molecular programs associated with parental, early gilteritinib-resistant, and late gilteritinib-resistant states, including altered signaling pathways, metabolic adaptation, and Aurora kinase B dependency in resistant cell populations.
Data_Caveats: The dataset is entirely based on acute myeloid leukemia cell line models and does not represent a clinical patient cohort. Samples correspond to experimentally induced parental, early resistant, and late resistant states in MOLM14 and MV411 leukemia cell lines under controlled in vitro conditions. Proteomic changes may therefore reflect cell culture adaptation and resistance modeling rather than in vivo tumor heterogeneity.

Title: The AML Microenvironment Catalyzes a Step-wise Evolution to Gilteritinib Resistance
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Cancer cell line: FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia MOLM14 cell line under parental control conditions and resistance-associated states induced by fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand stimulation
Disease Subtype: FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia with microenvironment-associated early resistance signaling induced by fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand
Experimental Design: TMT11-based proteome profiling of the FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia MOLM14 cell line under parental control conditions and resistance-associated states induced by fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand stimulation. The dataset includes longitudinal resistance-associated cellular states analyzed across multiple TMT11 plexes and fractionated liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry measurements.
Short Description: Proteomic characterization of parental and microenvironment-primed resistance-associated states in the FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia MOLM14 cell line.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteome profiling of the FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia MOLM14 cell line identified proteomic remodeling associated with fibroblast growth factor 2-primed and FLT3 ligand-primed resistance-associated states, including altered protein expression patterns linked to early resistance adaptation.
Data_Caveats: The dataset contains only proteome measurements from experimentally induced MOLM14 leukemia cell line resistance-associated states under controlled in vitro conditions and does not represent independent clinical patient-derived tumor samples.

Title: The AML Microenvironment Catalyzes a Step-wise Evolution to Gilteritinib Resistance
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia MOLM14 cell line under parental control conditions and quizartinib resistance-associated states induced by fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand stimulation
Disease Subtype: FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia with acquired resistance to quizartinib mediated by microenvironment-associated signaling
Experimental Design: TMT11-based proteome profiling of the FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia MOLM14 cell line under parental control conditions and quizartinib resistance-associated states induced by fibroblast growth factor 2 or FLT3 ligand stimulation, including late resistant leukemia cell populations analyzed by fractionated liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry across two TMT11 plexes.
Short Description: Proteomic characterization of parental and quizartinib resistance-associated states in the FLT3-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia MOLM14 cell line.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteome profiling identified distinct protein expression changes associated with fibroblast growth factor 2-induced and FLT3 ligand-induced quizartinib resistance-associated states, as well as stable proteomic remodeling in late quizartinib-resistant MOLM14 Acute Myeloid Leukemia cell populations.
Data_Caveats: The dataset contains only experimentally induced MOLM14 Acute Myeloid Leukemia cell line resistance-associated states analyzed under controlled in vitro conditions and does not include independent patient-derived tumor samples or healthy controls. Multiple annotation rows correspond to duplicated analytical measurements rather than independent biological samples.

Title: A Proteogenomic Portrait of Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary untreated lung squamous cell carcinoma tumor tissues and both matched (n = 99) and unmatched normal adjacent lung tissues.
Disease Subtype: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung belonging to the non-small cell lung cancer group
Experimental Design: Prospective Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium cohort with tandem mass tag 11-plex deep proteome profiling of primary untreated lung squamous cell carcinoma tumors and normal adjacent lung tissues, including 99 matched tumor–normal pairs, integrated with phosphoproteome, acetylproteome, ubiquitylome, whole-exome sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, ribonucleic acid sequencing, DNA methylation, imaging, and clinical annotation.
Short Description: Large-scale Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium proteogenomic characterization of lung squamous cell carcinoma integrating tandem mass tag 11-plex liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry proteomics with genomic, transcriptomic, DNA methylation, and post-translational modification analyses to identify molecular subtypes, immune states, signaling pathways, metabolic remodeling, therapeutic vulnerabilities, and candidate biomarkers associated with lung squamous cell carcinoma progression and treatment response.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic analysis identified five molecular subtypes of lung squamous cell carcinoma, including an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-enriched subtype with PDGFRB and ROR2 signaling activation, NSD3 as a candidate driver within FGFR1-amplified tumors, survivin overexpression in TP63-low tumors, SOX2-associated chromatin vulnerabilities involving LSD1 and EZH2, heterogeneous RB1 phosphorylation linked to cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitor response, and extensive immune and metabolic remodeling regulated through phosphorylation, acetylation, and ubiquitylation signaling networks.
Data_Caveats: The cohort included both matched and unmatched tumor and normal adjacent tissue samples, with fewer normal adjacent tissues than tumor samples, limiting fully paired tumor–normal comparisons across the complete dataset. Bulk tissue tandem mass tag proteomics may also obscure intratumoral heterogeneity and stromal contamination.

Title: Proteogenomic characterization of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumor tissue; normal adjacent pancreatic tissue; normal pancreatic duct tissue
Disease Subtype: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma
Experimental Design: TMT11-based proteome, phosphoproteome, and glycoproteome profiling of treatment-naive pancreatic tumors, adjacent normal pancreatic tissues, and normal pancreatic duct tissues integrated with whole-genome sequencing, whole-exome sequencing, RNA sequencing, microRNA sequencing, and DNA methylation analysis
Short Description: CPTAC multi-omics proteogenomic characterization of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma identifying molecular subtypes, glycoprotein biomarkers, kinase signaling vulnerabilities, immune microenvironment states, and candidate therapeutic targets
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT1 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic analysis identified PDAC molecular subtypes, glycoprotein biomarkers, kinase signaling vulnerabilities, immune-hot and immune-cold tumor microenvironment states, and candidate subtype-specific therapeutic targets
Data_Caveats: Low tumor purity, extensive stromal and acinar contamination, and strong tissue heterogeneity complicated PDAC proteome analysis. Additional bridge and reference tumor samples (KoreanReference and WU-PDA controls) were included for TMT inter-plex normalization, increasing technical aliquot counts beyond the biological cohort size.

Title: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic measurements enhance ability to predict ex vivo drug response in AML
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary AML patient-derived mononuclear/cancer cells from bone marrow and peripheral blood, including post-treatment samples
Disease Subtype: Primary AML blood/bone marrow cancer samples with ex vivo drug-response profiling; untreated and post-treatment samples
Experimental Design: TMT10-based LC–MS/MS global proteome profiling of primary AML patient-derived bone marrow and peripheral blood cancer samples from the Beat AML/PTRC cohort. Two baseline TMT10 plexes were analyzed with 24 fractions per plex; patient channels were quantified relative to reference channels.
Short Description: Proteomic profiling of primary AML patient samples to evaluate whether protein-level signatures improve prediction of ex vivo drug sensitivity, especially for targeted AML therapies such as quizartinib/FLT3 and trametinib/Ras–MEK pathway inhibition.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteomic profiling of primary AML patient-derived blood/bone marrow samples supported prediction of ex vivo drug sensitivity. Protein-level signatures were informative for AML drug-response modeling, especially for targeted agents such as quizartinib/FLT3 and trametinib/Ras–MEK pathway inhibition.
Data_Caveats: Small pilot proteome cohort; PDC000398 contains 16 patient samples in the TMT channel mapping, with no healthy controls. Untreated and post-treatment AML samples are mixed. Samples are primary patient-derived AML cells, not cell lines. Cell lines MOLM13/MOLM14 are discussed in the publication only as validation models, not as the main PDC000398 biospecimens.

Title: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic measurements enhance ability to predict ex vivo drug response in AML
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: AML patient-derived blood cancer cells; peripheral blood AML samples, including baseline and post-treatment aliquots
Disease Subtype: Acute myeloid leukemia; mainly AML with mutated NPM1, with one case annotated as acute myeloid leukemia with minimal differentiation
Experimental Design: TMT10-based global proteome profiling of AML patient-derived peripheral blood cancer samples in an ex vivo sorafenib-treatment drug-response setting. The dataset includes two TMT10 plexes, 12 fractions per plex, 4 biological AML patients, 16 AML aliquots, and Universal Ref channels for normalization.
Short Description: Small PTRC/Beat AML proteomics substudy measuring protein abundance in baseline and post-treatment AML peripheral blood-derived cancer samples to support analysis of ex vivo sorafenib-associated drug response.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteomic profiling of AML ex vivo sorafenib-treatment samples provides TMT10-based protein abundance data for drug-response signature analysis; broader PTRC/Beat AML analysis showed added predictive value of proteomic/phosphoproteomic measurements for AML drug sensitivity.
Data_Caveats: Small N; 4 AML patients plus Universal Ref; no healthy controls; no tumor-normal design; 16 samples are aliquots from 4 patients, not independent patients; post-treatment reflects ex vivo sorafenib exposure; Log Ratio/Unshared Log Ratio are duplicated metrics, not separate samples.

Title: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic measurements enhance ability to predict ex vivo drug response in AML
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: AML patient-derived leukemic mononuclear cells from bone marrow and peripheral blood
Disease Subtype: Acute myeloid leukemia; ex vivo combination-treatment drug-response cohort
Experimental Design: TMT11-based global proteome profiling of AML patient-derived blood and bone marrow cancer samples in an ex vivo combination-treatment drug-response study; 2 TMT11 plexes, 12 fractions per plex, 10 patient sample channels plus 1 universal reference channel per plex.
Short Description: Proteome dataset of AML patient-derived leukemic samples from bone marrow and peripheral blood, including baseline/untreated blood-derived cancer samples and post-treatment peripheral blood cancer samples, used to assess protein-level signatures associated with ex vivo response to combination drug treatment.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to pooled ref
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: TMT11 proteome profiling of AML patient-derived blood/bone marrow samples identified protein-level signatures associated with ex vivo response to combination drug treatment. The dataset supports evaluation of proteomic predictors of AML therapeutic sensitivity beyond clinical metadata alone.
Data_Caveats: Small pilot cohort; 20 patient sample channels but 19 unique patients/donors because 16-00278 is included in two TMT channels. Exposure status is inferred from PDC sample status: 5 post-treatment / combination-treatment exposed samples and 15 baseline / untreated sample channels. No healthy controls. Tumor grade, tumor stage, morphology and tumor classification are not reported. Universal reference channels are not patient samples.

Title: Proteogenomic markers of chemotherapy resistance and response in triple negative breast cancer
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Triple-negative breast cancer primary tumor tissue
Tumor Type: Triple-negative breast cancer; Breast invasive carcinoma
Experimental Design: TMT11-based proteome profiling of primary TNBC tumor tissues collected at baseline before neoadjuvant carboplatin/docetaxel therapy and, for a subset of patients, at Cycle 1 Day 3 after treatment initiation. The design used 8 TMT11 plexes with 72 fractions per plex and common reference channels.
Short Description: Proteomic analysis of primary TNBC tumor tissues to identify molecular features associated with response or resistance to neoadjuvant carboplatin/docetaxel therapy. Baseline tumor tissues represent untreated cancer samples; Cycle1Day3 tissues represent early on-treatment cancer samples.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteomic profiling of primary TNBC tumor tissues showed that chemotherapy-resistant / non-pCR tumors were enriched for metabolic programs, including oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism and glycolysis. Therapy-sensitive / pCR tumors showed higher DNA repair, E2F targets, G2/M checkpoint, interferon-gamma response and immune-checkpoint signatures. Proteogenomic analysis identified a resistance-associated 19q13.31–33 deletion involving LIG1, POLD1 and XRCC1; low LIG1 / LIG1 loss was linked to poor pathological response, chromosomal instability and carboplatin-selective resistance.
Data_Caveats: Dataset contains tumor tissues only; no healthy controls and no matched normal breast tissue. Baseline samples are untreated tumor tissues, while Cycle1Day3 samples are early on-treatment tumor tissues after carboplatin/docetaxel initiation. Reference channels Core CR and Pros BRCA CR should not be counted as patient samples. Some patients have both baseline and Cycle1Day3 samples, so aliquot/sample count exceeds patient count.

Title: Neoplastic cell enrichment of tumor tissues using coring and laser microdissection for proteomic and genomic analyses of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumor tissues and matched normal adjacent pancreatic tissues processed using bulk sampling, tissue coring, and laser microdissection (LMD)
Disease Subtype: PDAC with variable neoplastic cellularity and stromal composition
Experimental Design: TMT10-based quantitative proteomics and whole-exome sequencing of PDAC tumors and matched normal adjacent tissues processed using bulk sampling, tissue coring, and laser microdissection (LMD) to evaluate neoplastic cell enrichment effects on proteogenomic profiling
Short Description: Comparative proteogenomic study assessing how bulk tissue sampling, coring, and laser microdissection influence tumor cellularity, KRAS mutation enrichment, and proteomic composition in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Laser microdissection (LMD) provided the strongest enrichment of neoplastic cellularity and produced the most distinct proteomic profile compared with bulk and cored PDAC tissues. Bulk and coring samples showed highly similar proteomic patterns, while LMD improved KRAS mutation enrichment, especially in low-cellularity tumors. Distinct PDAC-associated proteins including COL17A1, VSNL1, LYPD3, and VCAN were preferentially identified in LMD-enriched samples.
Data_Caveats: Small cohort size with only 3 paired PDAC/NAT cases for proteomics and 8 tumors for KRAS/WES validation limits statistical power. Bulk tumors contained substantial stromal and non-neoplastic contamination due to highly variable tumor cellularity characteristic of PDAC. Sampling strategy strongly affected detected protein composition, complicating interpretation of tumor-specific signals. Coring failed to effectively enrich neoplastic cells in low-cellularity tumors, whereas LMD produced limited material yield and may introduce preparation-related bias. Metadata structure in PDC incompletely annotates sampling strategy and replicate relationships.

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of lung adenocarcinoma reveals tumor heterogeneity, survival determinants, and therapeutically relevant pathways
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissue
Disease Subtype: Primary lung adenocarcinoma; LUAD molecular/expression subtypes including TRU, PI and PP
Experimental Design: TMT11-based proteome profiling of primary LUAD tumor tissues, integrated in the study with WGS, RNA-seq, phosphoproteomics and RPPA
Short Description: Proteogenomic study of primary lung adenocarcinoma tumors identifying molecular heterogeneity, RNA–protein relationships, survival-associated protein/RNA signatures and subtype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteogenomic profiling of LUAD identified molecular heterogeneity, smoking-associated genomic subtypes, RNA/protein survival signatures, and subtype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities including immune-checkpoint, EGFR-signaling, cell-cycle and metabolic pathways.
Data_Caveats: No matched normal lung proteome was analyzed in this proteome dataset; treatment-response data were limited; PDC lists 101 cases/aliquots, but the usable tumor cohort in the article is 87 cases and the annotation table contains duplicated tumor entries plus a Pool/reference entry.

Title: Proteogenomic landscape of human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in an Asian population reveals tumor cell-enriched and immune-rich subtypes
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumor tissue
Disease Subtype: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in an Asian patient cohort with tumor cell-enriched and immune-rich molecular subtypes
Experimental Design: TMT10-based global proteome profiling of primary pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumor tissues using two-dimensional liquid chromatography and Orbitrap mass spectrometry integrated with whole-exome sequencing and RNA sequencing
Short Description: Large-scale Asian pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma proteogenomic study integrating TMT10 LC-MS/MS proteomics with genomic and transcriptomic profiling to define molecular subtypes, immune composition, and signaling pathway alterations
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic analysis identified tumor cell-enriched and immune-rich pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma subtypes and revealed associations between genomic alterations, proteomic signaling pathways, and immune microenvironment composition linked to potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.
Data_Caveats: Proteome dataset contains only tumor tissues without matched healthy pancreatic controls in the PDC proteome cohort; TMT-based relative quantification may be affected by ratio compression and batch effects associated with pooled reference normalization.

Title: Refining Classification of Cholangiocarcinoma Subtypes via Proteogenomic Integration Reveals New Therapeutic Prospects
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma tumor tissues and adjacent non-tumorous liver tissues
Disease Subtype: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma classified into stem-like, poorly immunogenic, and metabolism subtypes
Experimental Design: TMT10-based proteome and phosphoproteome profiling of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma tissues integrated with whole-exome sequencing, RNA-seq, metabolomics, and organoid validation; proteome + phosphoproteome; LC-MS/MS; WES; RNA-seq; organoid models
Short Description: Multi-omics characterization of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma identifying clinically distinct proteogenomic subtypes associated with stemness, immune suppression, metabolic remodeling, and therapeutic vulnerabilities including ALDH1A1-targeted strategies
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteogenomic analysis identified three clinically distinct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma subtypes associated with stemness, immune suppression, and metabolic remodeling. ALDH1A1 overexpression characterized the stem-like subtype, and ALDH1A1 inhibition synergized with nab-paclitaxel in organoid models. Multi-omics integration refined molecular stratification beyond transcriptomics alone and revealed subtype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities.
Data_Caveats: PDC metadata contains heterogeneous annotations including reference/disqualified samples and non-iCC labels despite the study focus on intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Sample numbers differed across proteome, transcriptome, phosphoproteome, and WES datasets. Adjacent non-tumorous tissues rather than independent healthy controls were used. TMT-based relative quantification may introduce ratio compression. Cohort consisted predominantly of Asian patients, which may limit population generalizability.

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of chemo-refractory high-grade serous ovarian cancer
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma tumor tissues from female patients with stage II–IV disease
Experimental Design: TMT11-based LC-MS/MS global proteome profiling of pre-treatment FFPE primary HGSOC tumor tissues
Short Description: FFPE validation proteome cohort of primary untreated HGSOC tumor samples analyzed using CPTAC harmonized TMT11 proteomics workflow
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; FFPE-adjusted norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding:
Main_Finding	Data_Caveats
TMT11-based proteome profiling of pre-treatment FFPE HGSOC tumors supported identification and validation of protein signatures, pathway-level stratification, and molecular features associated with platinum-refractory ovarian cancer, including metabolic, immune, hypoxia, EMT, and TGF-β-associated proteomic states
Data_Caveats: Small FFPE validation cohort; archival FFPE material may reduce proteome and post-translational modification coverage; proteomic associations are correlative and derived from pre-treatment bulk tumor tissues with substantial biological heterogeneity

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of chemo-refractory high-grade serous ovarian cancer
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma tumor tissues from female patients with stage II–IV disease
Experimental Design: TMT11-based LC-MS/MS global proteome profiling of pre-treatment FFPE primary HGSOC tumor tissues
Short Description: FFPE validation proteome cohort of primary untreated HGSOC tumor samples analyzed using CPTAC harmonized TMT11 proteomics workflow
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; FFPE-adjusted norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Large-scale TMT11 proteome profiling of treatment-naive FFPE HGSOC tumors identified proteomic subtypes and molecular programs associated with platinum refractoriness, including immune remodeling, extracellular matrix organization, EMT, hypoxia, metabolism, and TGF-β signaling, and enabled development of a 64-protein predictive signature
Data_Caveats: FFPE archival tissue may reduce proteome and PTM coverage; cohort includes both primary and metastatic lesions with substantial biological heterogeneity; analyses are observational and derived from bulk tumor proteomes rather than therapy-perturbation experiments

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of chemo-refractory high-grade serous ovarian cancer
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary frozen high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma tumor tissues from female patients with stage II–IV disease
Experimental Design: TMT11-based LC-MS/MS global proteome profiling of pre-treatment frozen HGSOC tumor tissues using CPTAC harmonized workflow
Short Description: Frozen validation proteome cohort of untreated HGSOC tumors analyzed to validate proteomic molecular features and platinum-response-associated signatures identified in the discovery cohort
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Frozen-tissue TMT11 proteome profiling validated proteomic programs and molecular signatures associated with platinum refractoriness in HGSOC, including immune remodeling, extracellular matrix organization, EMT, hypoxia, and metabolic pathway alterations identified in the discovery cohort
Data_Caveats: Cohort consists of heterogeneous bulk tumor tissues from advanced-stage HGSOC patients; analyses are observational and based on pre-treatment samples without therapy perturbation; partial overlap with the discovery cohort may reduce complete external independence of validation

Title: Proteogenomic insights suggest druggable pathways in endometrial carcinoma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary endometrial carcinoma tumor tissue and solid normal endometrial tissue
Disease Subtype: Endometrioid, serous, clear cell; molecular/genomic subtypes: POLE ultramutated, MSI-H, CNV-L, CNV-H
Experimental Design: Prospective CPTAC proteogenomic study of 138 endometrial carcinoma tumors and 20 enriched normal endometrium samples using 10 omics platforms: WGS, WES, methylation array, RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, targeted proteomics, global proteomics, phosphoproteomics, acetylproteomics, and glycoproteomics
Short Description: Comprehensive proteogenomic analysis of an independent endometrial carcinoma cohort identifying clinically relevant molecular and imaging markers, including APM/SRM markers for immunotherapy stratification, PIK3R1 in-frame indels associated with AKT phosphorylation and AKT inhibitor sensitivity, MYC activity as a potential biomarker of metformin response, CTNNB1 hotspot mutations affecting Wnt/β-catenin signaling, PARP1/1q gain as a possible PARP inhibitor biomarker, and deep-learning prediction of EC subtypes from histopathology images.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: The study identified clinically relevant molecular and imaging markers for precision stratification of endometrial carcinoma, including: SRM-based APM markers for potential immunotherapy selection; PIK3R1 in-frame indels associated with increased AKT phosphorylation and sensitivity to AKT inhibitors; high MYC activity as a potential biomarker for metformin response; CTNNB1 hotspot mutations linked to altered Wnt/β-catenin signaling and possible resistance to Wnt-FZD antagonists; 1q/PARP1 gain as a possible biomarker of PARP inhibitor sensitivity; and deep-learning prediction of EC molecular subtypes and mutations from histopathology images.
Data_Caveats: Prospective CPTAC cohort with 140 EC tumors and 20 enriched normal endometrium samples; normal tissues were enriched normal endometrium from healthy donors, not necessarily matched adjacent normals for every tumor. Several therapeutic conclusions are biomarker-generating and require further clinical validation, especially SRM/APM prediction, MYC–metformin response, AKT inhibitor sensitivity for PIK3R1 indels, PARP inhibitor sensitivity for PARP1/1q gain, and histopathology deep-learning models

Title: Integrated proteogenomic characterization of glioblastoma evolution
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary glioblastoma tumor tissue; recurrent glioblastoma tumor tissue; paired longitudinal tumor tissue
Disease Subtype: Glioblastoma multiforme; longitudinal primary and recurrent glioblastoma
Experimental Design: TMT11-based LC-MS/MS global proteome profiling of glioblastoma tissue samples collected at diagnosis and recurrence; primary and recurrent tumor samples were quantified relative to pooled reference channels across TMT11 plexes.
Short Description: Global proteome dataset comparing primary glioblastoma tumors collected at diagnosis with recurrent glioblastoma tumors collected after treatment.
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Global proteome analysis showed that primary glioblastoma tumors are enriched in proliferation-, cell-cycle-, DNA replication- and EGFR-related programs, whereas recurrent tumors show increased abundance of proteins associated with neuronal transition, synaptic activity and neuron-like functions. Proteomic data also indicated reduced EGFR protein/signaling at recurrence and increased activity of BRAF/MAPK- and WNT/PCP-related proteins, supporting a shift from proliferative primary GBM toward a neuronal recurrent state.
Data_Caveats: Proteome-only dataset; no healthy brain tissue controls or adjacent normal tissue were included. Recurrent tumors are post-treatment samples, so proteomic differences may reflect both tumor evolution and therapy-associated selection. Reference/pool channels are technical normalization references, not biological controls. The publication reports a larger integrative cohort, while the proteome analysis was performed on a subset of longitudinal GBM pairs.

Title: Mapping the proteogenomic landscape enables prediction of drug response in acute myeloid leukemia
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Freshly isolated primary acute myeloid leukemia blasts; mononuclear leukemia cells
Tissue: Bone marrow; peripheral blood; leukapheresis sample
Tumor Type: Acute myeloid leukemia; myelodysplastic syndromes; non-specified leukemia cases included in the cohort
Disease Subtype: Acute myeloid leukemia; myelodysplastic syndromes; non-specified leukemia cases included in the cohort
Experimental Design: Tandem mass tag 11-plex global proteome profiling of primary patient-derived leukemia cells by liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry; paired phosphoproteome data were generated in the related study; proteomic data were integrated in the article with whole-exome sequencing, RNA sequencing, clinical annotation and ex vivo drug sensitivity screening across small-molecule inhibitors
Short Description: Proteogenomic study of primary acute myeloid leukemia patient samples from the Beat AML cohort. The study used proteome and phosphoproteome measurements to define four proteogenomic leukemia subtypes, compare them with genetic classifications, and link subtype structure to ex vivo drug-response patterns, including response models for venetoclax, panobinostat and other inhibitors. PDC000477 represents the global proteome component of the study
Normalization Strategy: CDAP pipeline; median normalization; log2 ratio to pooled ref
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Tandem mass tag 11-plex proteomic profiling of primary patient-derived acute myeloid leukemia cells identified four proteogenomic leukemia subtypes that complemented genomic mutation-based classification and were associated with distinct ex vivo drug-response patterns. The study measured 9,412 unique proteins, retained 8,521 proteins after missingness filtering, and used corrected proteomic and phosphoproteomic data to classify 210 patient samples. Proteomic subtype information improved interpretation of drug sensitivity, including venetoclax, panobinostat and sorafenib response patterns, and supported models for predicting therapy response.
Data_Caveats: PDC000477 represents the global proteome component only; several biological conclusions in the article rely on integration with the related phosphoproteome study, transcriptomics, whole-exome sequencing, clinical annotation and ex vivo drug-response data. PDC reports 211 cases and 211 aliquots, whereas the article analyzes 210 patient samples; the uploaded annotation contains 378 rows and gives 189 deduplicated sample entries by sample type, so sample accounting differs across PDC metadata, annotation rows and article-level cohort description. The cohort consists of bulk primary leukemia cell preparations, so clonal heterogeneity and variation in leukemic versus stromal cell composition are not resolved. The study is also limited by single-time-point profiling for most patient samples, while dynamic treatment-response conclusions are supported mainly by MOLM14 cell-line validation rather than longitudinal patient sampling.

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of enriched HGSOC tumor epithelium identifies prognostic signatures and therapeutic vulnerabilities
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Bulk high-grade serous carcinoma tumor tissue; laser microdissection-enriched high-grade serous carcinoma tumor epithelium; laser microdissection-enriched stromal compartment in a subset.
Tissue: High-grade serous carcinoma tumor tissue from ovary, peritoneum, and abdominal/metastatic sites.
Disease Subtype: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC; APOLLO-2 cohort)
Experimental Design: TMT11-based global proteome profiling of untreated high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma tumors, including matched bulk tumor tissue and laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelial fractions; integrated with whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, reverse phase protein array data, tumor purity assessment, homologous recombination deficiency/proficiency classification, and survival analysis.
Short Description: Proteogenomic study of 70 chemo-naive high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma tumors from primary/adnexal and metastatic sites. The study compared bulk tumor tissue with laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelium to evaluate how tumor purity, stromal admixture, immune infiltration, molecular subtype reclassification, homologous recombination deficiency-associated metabolic pathways, and BMI1 expression relate to prognosis and therapeutic vulnerability. Стромальные фракции анализировались только в subset, поэтому в краткое описание можно добавить, но не считать их отдельной основной группой samples.
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelium increased tumor purity and improved detection of somatic variants, structural variants, and predicted neoepitopes compared with bulk tumor. Bulk mesenchymal subtype calls were strongly affected by stromal admixture and often changed after epithelial enrichment. Longer progression-free survival was associated with immune/TIL-related proteomic signatures. HRD tumors showed enrichment of mitochondrial metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. HRP tumors showed elevated BMI1; high BMI1 correlated with poorer outcome in HRP tumors, and HRP HGSOC cells were more sensitive to BMI1 inhibitors
Data_Caveats: Main analytical cohort contains 70 chemo-naive HGSOC tumors, although PDC metadata may include duplicated sample-level entries and non-biological/service entries such as Pool/Withheld. Samples are tumor-only: no healthy controls or precancer samples. The study includes both bulk tumor and laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelial fractions; stromal fractions were analyzed only in a subset and should not be counted as a separate main sample group. Tumor purity, stromal admixture, immune-cell admixture, and primary versus metastatic site can strongly affect interpretation. Some reported validations use independent cohorts and cell-line BMI1 inhibitor assays, not the primary TMT11 APOLLO-OV proteome cohort

Title: Comprehensive proteogenomic characterization of rare kidney tumors
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary kidney tumor tissue and adjacent normal kidney tissue from renal cell carcinoma cohort
Tumor Type: Non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma; renal oncocytoma; other rare renal tumors
Disease Subtype: Non-clear cell kidney cancer; clear cell kidney cancer; papillary kidney cancer; chromophobe kidney cancer; renal oncocytoma; other rare kidney tumors
Experimental Design: Tandem mass tag 11-plex proteome profiling using liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry; integrated with phosphoproteome, glycoproteome, metabolome, genome, transcriptome, methylation and single-nucleus transcriptome data
Short Description: Proteomic analysis of rare kidney tumors and non-clear cell kidney cancer subtypes to compare protein abundance profiles between tumor subtypes and adjacent normal tissue, define subtype-specific proteomic signatures, and identify candidate diagnostic and prognostic protein biomarkers.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: TMT11 proteomic profiling identified subtype-specific protein abundance patterns in rare kidney tumors. The study detected 12,299 proteins, with 9,528 proteins quantified in more than half of samples, and showed clear proteomic separation between tumor subtypes and normal adjacent tissues. Key protein biomarkers included PYCR1 and IGF2BP3 for genome instability, MAPRE3 and ADGRF5 for renal oncocytoma, GPNMB for chromophobe kidney cancer, and PIGR and SOSTDC1 for papillary kidney cancer.
Data_Caveats: Proteomic dataset is limited by small sample size for several rare kidney tumor subtypes, with some subtypes represented by only one or two samples. PDC000464 contains the proteome component, while several conclusions in the article rely on integration with additional omics layers and related cohorts. Therefore, subtype-specific proteomic biomarkers and pathway signatures should be considered exploratory and require validation in independent cohorts.

Title: Multi-scale signaling and tumor evolution in high-grade gliomas
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Brain tumor tissue; glioblastoma / glioma tissue; includes primary and recurrent tumor tissue; some metastatic brain-resected tumor samples
Disease: Glioblastoma; Gliomas; Astrocytoma; Gliosarcoma; Meningioma; brain metastases
Disease Subtype: High-grade glioma; primary GBM; recurrent GBM; IDH-mutant/IDH-wildtype status when available; brain metastases from lung, breast, uterus, colon/other primary sites
Experimental Design: TMT11-based LC–MS/MS proteome profiling of CPTAC GBM confirmatory samples; 24 fractions per TMT plex; channels include pooled reference, primary tumors, recurrent tumors, metastatic brain-resected tumors, and solid tissue normal controls
Short Description: Proteomic profiling of GBM/high-grade glioma cohort with primary and recurrent tumor specimens, limited normal brain tissue controls, and a subset of brain metastasis samples. The study is designed to characterize tumor evolution, recurrence-associated proteomic changes, and molecular heterogeneity in glioblastoma.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: The study identifies proteomic features associated with GBM biology and tumor evolution, including differences between primary and recurrent tumors, recurrence-related signaling changes, IDH-associated molecular differences, and pathway-level alterations involving RTK signaling, EGFR, PTEN/TERT-related downstream effects, and PTPN11-centered signaling networks.
Data_Caveats: The proteome cohort is heterogeneous: it includes primary GBM/high-grade glioma samples, recurrent tumors, limited solid tissue normal controls, and brain metastasis samples from non-GBM primary cancers. Treatment/exposure information is not available for all samples in the channel mapping table; it appears mainly in the clinical annotation for a subset of recurrent/CHOP retrospective cases. Therefore, treatment-related conclusions should be made only for samples with explicit treatment metadata, not for the entire TMT proteome cohort.

Title: Integrated multi-omics analyses of oral squamous cell carcinoma reveal precision patient stratification and personalized treatment strategies
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary oral squamous cell carcinoma tumor tissue; paired/adjacent solid normal oral cavity tissue; pooled tissue internal reference; pooled cell-line internal reference
Tissue: Oral cavity tumor tissue; oral cavity solid normal tissue; subsites include tongue, cheek mucosa, gum, floor of mouth, retromolar area, lip
Tumor Type: Oral squamous cell carcinoma; primary sites include tongue, cheek mucosa, gum, floor of mouth, retromolar area, and lip.
Disease Subtype: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, oral cavity; squamous cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified; A3A/EGFR-stratified OSCC groups
Experimental Design: TMT10-based proteomic profiling of pretreatment OSCC tumor tissues and solid normal tissue samples from oral cavity subsites, including tongue, cheek mucosa, gum, floor of mouth, retromolar area, and lip; tumor samples were stratified by A3A/APOBEC3A and EGFR expression and integrated with RNA-seq, whole-exome sequencing/copy-number alteration analysis, phosphoproteomics, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, cell-based assays, and PDX validation
Short Description: Integrated multi-omics study of OSCC identifying inverse A3A/APOBEC3A and EGFR expression as patient-stratification markers. A3A-high tumors were associated with immune-hot phenotype and anti-PD-1 response, whereas EGFR-high and RRAS-high tumors were linked to DNA repair alterations, EGFR/RRAS/AKT/ERK signaling, local recurrence, and potential anti-EGFR treatment relevance
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: A3A/APOBEC3A and EGFR were identified as inversely expressed RNA/protein-level markers for OSCC patient stratification. A3A-high tumors showed immune-hot features and were associated with improved anti-PD-1 response, whereas EGFR-high tumors showed chromosome 7p11.2 gains and DNA repair alterations. RRAS-high tumors were linked to local recurrence through EGFR/RRAS/AKT/ERK signaling and AKT/ERK phosphorylation, suggesting potential relevance for anti-EGFR treatment response.
Data_Caveats: PDC000519 is the proteome study; phosphoproteome data are related but separate PDC projects. The dataset includes primary tumor, solid normal tissue, pooled tissue internal reference, and pooled cell-line internal reference channels; reference channels should not be interpreted as patient samples. Several tumor/normal biospecimens are marked as disqualified and should be excluded from biological interpretation. Clinical metadata are incomplete for several fields, with many values reported as “Not Reported

Title: Proteogenomic characterization of molecular and cellular targets for treatment-resistant subtypes in locally advanced cervical cancers
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary locally advanced cervical cancer tumor tissues including squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and adenosquamous carcinoma.
Tumor Type: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma; endocervical adenocarcinoma; adenosquamous carcinoma
Disease Subtype: Locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC); squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and adenosquamous carcinoma
Experimental Design: TMT11-based global proteome and phosphoproteome profiling integrated with whole-exome sequencing, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq for molecular characterization of treatment-resistant locally advanced cervical cancer subtypes
Short Description: Multi-omics characterization of locally advanced cervical cancer identified six molecular subtypes associated with treatment resistance, stromal activation, immune suppression, EMT remodeling, and mucin glycosylation
Normalization Strategy: N/A — no processed mass spectra in PDC
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Global proteome and phosphoproteome profiling identified treatment-resistant cervical cancer subtypes associated with stromal activation, EMT remodeling, immune suppression, and mucin O-glycosylation signatures
Data_Caveats: Proteome cohort included only tumor tissues without matched normal controls; proteomics was available for only 146–150  tumors from the full cohort; strong stromal and immune cell infiltration may influence bulk protein abundance profiles; substantial histological heterogeneity between squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and adenosquamous carcinoma; subtype associations are largely correlative rather than mechanistically validate. The study identified elevated expression of MUC5AC-associated epithelial populations together with enrichment of mucin O-glycosylation pathways in treatment-resistant adenocarcinoma-enriched tumors. Cohort consisted predominantly of Asian patients, which may limit population generalizability. Subtype associations were largely correlative rather than mechanistically validated.

Title: Proteogenomic characterization of non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors unravels clinically relevant subgroups
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Well-differentiated non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor tissue; matched pancreatic solid normal tissue
Tissue: Primary pancreatic tumor tissue; matched pancreatic solid normal tissue
Experimental Design: TMT16-based global proteome profiling of primary NF-PanNET tumor tissue and matched pancreatic solid normal tissue; MS2 reporter-ion quantification; trypsin digestion; iodoacetamide alkylation; bRPLC/RPLC fractionation; Q Exactive HF-X; DDA-HCD acquisition
Short Description: Proteome PhaseII arm of a proteogenomic NF-PanNET discovery study. The usable pancreatic cohort in this PDC part includes paired primary pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and matched solid normal pancreatic tissue; the broader study integrates genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic and phosphoproteomic data to define molecular subgroups, prognostic proteins and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT16 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic analysis of NF-PanNETs identified functional effects of recurrent driver alterations, especially MEN1-related changes; a three-protein prognostic signature; four proteomic/phosphoproteomic molecular subtypes with distinct immune and clinicopathological features; and candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities, including CDK5 and CACNA1D/CACNA4D-related subtype-specific targeting.
Data_Caveats: PDC000588 is only the Proteome PhaseII part of the broader Cancer Cell 2025 study, not the whole 108-case multi-omic article. PDC lists 53 cases / 94 aliquots, but many samples in the export are Disqualified or Not Reported; for clean pancreatic tumor–normal proteome analysis, use only the non-disqualified pancreatic pairs. The usable tumor samples are well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, mostly G1/G2, with matched pancreatic solid normal tissue.

Title: Proteogenomic characterization of non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors unravels clinically relevant subgroups
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary NF-PanNET tumor tissue and matched/adjacent normal pancreatic tissue
Tumor Type: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor / well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
Disease Subtype: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors / NF-PanNETs; mostly well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, G1–G
Experimental Design: TMT11-based global proteome profiling of primary NF-PanNET tumors and matched/adjacent normal pancreatic tissues; isobaric MS2 reporter ion quantitation, 2D-LC-MS/MS, DDA on Q Exactive HF-X
Short Description: Proteome Phase I discovery cohort for molecular characterization of NF-PanNETs. Dataset includes pancreatic primary tumor and solid tissue normal samples; used to support proteomic stratification, prognostic protein signatures, and therapeutic vulnerability analysis
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteome profiling of NF-PanNET supports molecular stratification of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and helps identify prognosis-associated protein signatures and potential therapeutic vulnerabilities. The broader study description reports proteomic/phosphoproteomic subtype analysis, a three-protein prognostic signature, and candidate targets including CDK5 and CACNA4D.
Data_Caveats: PDC000590 is Proteome Phase I only. Although the study description mentions genomics, transcriptomics, phosphoproteomics, mouse models, PDOs and xenografts, these are not all contained in this PDC entry. Biospecimens include Primary Tumor and Solid Tissue Normal pancreas samples, plus M1–M23 Not Reported / Other samples. Clinical metadata describe NF-PanNET cases, mostly well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with grades G1–G3 and stages I–IV, but part of cases have grade/stage/morphology as Not Reported. Some samples are marked Disqualified, so counts should be checked separately for total vs usable samples

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of the CALGB 40601 (Alliance) HER2+ breast cancer
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Pretreatment needle-core biopsies from primary HER2-positive breast invasive carcinoma tumors; fresh-frozen OCT-embedded tumor tissue; no cell lines; no mouse samples.
Disease Subtype: HER2-positive breast cancer; neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy cohort
Experimental Design: TMT16-based proteomic analysis of pretreatment primary tumor biopsies from patients with HER2-positive breast cancer enrolled in the CALGB 40601 neoadjuvant trial. The PDC proteome dataset includes 59 cases and 80 aliquots, analyzed across 5 TMT16 plexes with 24 fractions per plex. The study was designed to identify protein-level biomarkers associated with pathological complete response versus non-pCR after anti-HER2 therapy
Short Description: Proteomic profiling of pretreatment HER2-positive breast cancer biopsies from the CALGB 40601 trial identified resistance-associated features, including lack of ERBB2 amplification/HER2 protein overexpression in some non-pCR cases and increased EMT, Notch, and WNT/β-catenin signaling in non-pCR tumors. GPRC5A and TPBG were validated as reproducible markers associated with lack of pathological complete response.
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT16 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteogenomic profiling of pretreatment HER2-positive breast cancer biopsies identified molecular features associated with resistance to neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy. Non-pCR tumors included cases lacking ERBB2 amplification and HER2 protein overexpression, suggesting possible false HER2-positive classification by standard diagnostics. In proteogenomics-confirmed HER2-positive tumors, non-pCR was associated with increased EMT, Notch, WNT/β-catenin and extracellular matrix/tumor microenvironment-related signaling. GPRC5A and TPBG were validated across independent datasets as reproducible markers of lack of pathological complete response.
Data_Caveats: This proteome dataset contains tumor biopsies only: no healthy controls and no normal adjacent tissue. PDC reports 59 cases and 80 aliquots, while the article states that 75 of 80 QC-passed biopsies yielded TMT-based proteomic/phosphoproteomic data. Several patients had 1–2 biopsies, so case count and biopsy/aliquot count differ. The PDC proteome study is linked to a separate phosphoproteome study, PDC000583. The study is response-focused and correlative, with limited sample size per treatment arm.

Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary LUAD tumor tissues and normal adjacent tissues (NAT); partially paired cohort
Experimental Design: TMT10-based proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylproteome, and ubiquitylome profiling of LUAD tumors and NAT controls with pooled CompRef channel, integrated with WXS, RNA-seq, and DNA methylation
Short Description: Large-scale CPTAC LUAD proteogenomic study integrating TMT10 LC-MS/MS proteomics with genomic and epigenomic profiling to characterize molecular heterogeneity, carcinogen exposure signatures, KRAS/EGFR-associated pathways, chromosomal instability, PTM remodeling, and immune signaling differences across diverse populations
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic analysis identified lung adenocarcinoma molecular subtypes associated with KRAS and epidermal growth factor receptor signaling, carcinogen exposure signatures, chromosomal instability, post-translational modification remodeling, immune signaling alterations, and early-stage tumors with advanced molecular features.
Data_Caveats: PDC000153 contains only the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium lung adenocarcinoma discovery proteome cohort and not the full integrated multi-ethnic 2025 study cohort; normal adjacent tissue samples were available only for a subset of tumors, and bulk tissue tandem mass tag profiling may obscure intratumoral heterogeneity and cell-type-specific proteomic signals.

Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissue and matched normal adjacent tissue
Disease Subtype: Non-small cell lung cancer adenocarcinoma from Taiwanese patients
Experimental Design: Tandem mass tag 10-plex global proteome profiling with liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry, whole exome sequencing, and ribonucleic acid sequencing
Short Description: Proteogenomic profiling of Taiwanese lung adenocarcinoma tumors and matched normal adjacent lung tissues using tandem mass tag 10-plex liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry integrated with genomic and transcriptomic analyses to characterize ethnicity-specific molecular subtypes, smoking-associated alterations, epidermal growth factor receptor signaling, and mutational processes associated with apolipoprotein B messenger ribonucleic acid editing catalytic polypeptide-like enzymes.
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Taiwanese lung adenocarcinoma demonstrated distinct proteogenomic subtypes associated with smoking exposure, epidermal growth factor receptor alterations, apolipoprotein B messenger ribonucleic acid editing catalytic polypeptide-like mutagenesis, immune remodeling, and metabolic pathway dysregulation linked to tumor progression and clinical outcome.
Data_Caveats: The dataset contains relative tandem mass tag reporter ion quantification with pooled reference normalization rather than absolute protein abundance values; several quality control pooled samples and non-lung adenocarcinoma annotations remain present in metadata tables; five low-quality or corrupted raw mass spectrometry files were removed and one replacement raw data file was added in study version 2.

Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissue; matched normal adjacent lung tissue; internal reference/control samples
Tumor Type: Lung tumor tissue; normal adjacent lung tissue
Experimental Design: TMT11-based LC-MS/MS proteome profiling of primary lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissues and matched normal adjacent lung tissues; pooled/internal reference samples were included for cross-plex normalization; data are part of the CPTAC LUAD Confirmatory proteome cohort and were integrated with genomic and transcriptomic data in the broader CPTAC–ICPC LUAD study.
Short Description: CPTAC LUAD Confirmatory proteome dataset containing lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissues, matched normal adjacent lung tissues, and internal reference/control samples; used in a larger 406-patient proteogenomic LUAD analysis across diverse ethnicities and environmental exposures.
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated LUAD proteogenomic analysis identified molecular heterogeneity associated with driver mutations, chromosomal instability, immune signaling, carcinogen exposure signatures, and early-stage tumors with late-like molecular features; candidate protein biomarkers were proposed for genome-fragmented tumors and carcinogen-associated LUAD.
Data_Caveats: PDC000489 represents only the CPTAC LUAD Confirmatory proteome component of the broader CPTAC–ICPC LUAD integration; the full publication also includes other related LUAD projects, including CPTAC Discovery and Academia Sinica/ICPC cohorts. Therefore, conclusions from the 406-patient study should not be attributed only to PDC000489. In addition, PDC000489 contains internal reference/control/bridging entries, so biological LUAD patient samples must be separated from technical/reference samples

Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissue — 98; matched solid normal lung tissue from lung adenocarcinoma cases — 98; primary lung squamous cell carcinoma tumor tissue — 13; matched solid normal lung tissue from lung squamous cell carcinoma cases — 13; other primary lung tumor tissue — 13; matched solid normal lung tissue from other lung tumor cases — 13.
Tissue: Lung tumor tissue; normal adjacent lung tissue
Tumor Type: Lung adenocarcinoma; lung squamous cell carcinoma; other lung tumor
Disease Subtype: Non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma (Asian/Taiwanese cohort B)
Experimental Design: TMT10-based quantitative proteome profiling of paired lung tumor and matched solid normal lung tissue samples from the Academia Sinica LUAD ICPC-B cohort. The biospecimen table contains 248 unique tissue samples: 124 primary tumors and 124 matched solid normal lung tissues, including 98 lung adenocarcinoma cases, 13 lung squamous cell carcinoma cases and 13 other lung tumor cases.
Short Description: CGU OSCC APOBEC3A proteome dataset; PDC000519; TMT10 oral squamous cell carcinoma tissue proteome study with 224 tumor/normal tissue samples in the curated annotation: 112 primary tumors and 112 matched solid normal oral tissues, plus pooled internal reference entries.
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteomic profiling of oral squamous cell carcinoma identified APOBEC3A-associated molecular features and supported integrative tumor–normal comparison in OSCC tissue samples. The dataset provides a TMT10 proteome resource for studying OSCC biology, tumor-associated protein alterations, and APOBEC3A-related proteomic patterns.
Data_Caveats: PDC000563 represents the Academia Sinica LUAD ICPC-B proteome component, but the associated publication integrates multiple related PDC datasets from CPTAC and ICPC Academia Sinica programs. Therefore, conclusions from the paper refer to the broader 406-patient multi-cohort LUAD analysis, not only to PDC000563. Related studies include CPTAC LUAD proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome and ubiquitylome datasets, as well as Academia Sinica LUAD100 proteome/phosphoproteome and ICPC-B phosphoproteome datasets. Taiwanese IR was used as a bridging internal reference for cross-cohort comparison. For the curated biospecimen count, use the project-level tissue annotation separately from the publication-level integrated cohort size.

Title: Nicotine-induced protein expression profiling reveals mutually altered proteins across four human cell lines
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Embryonic kidney (HEK293); Cervical adenocarcinoma (HeLa); Pancreatic stellate cells (RLT-PSC); Bone marrow-derived neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y)
Experimental Design: Drug-treatment (Nicotine), TMT 10-plex, SPS-MS3, Multi-cell line comparison Mock-treatment (sterile water); Orbitrap Fusion
Short Description: The study quantified 8590 proteins across four human cell lines (HEK, HeLa, PaSC, SH-SY5Y), each mock- or nicotine-treated, using TMT 10-plex and SPS-MS3 to profile nicotine-induced proteomic alterations.
Normalization Strategy: Protein abundance values are normalized TMT reporter ion signal/count values. Reporter ion channels were summed across all quantified proteins and normalized assuming equal protein loading across all ten TMT samples. Derived log2 columns represent log2(nicotine-treated / mock-treated) ratios calculated from the normalized abundance values.
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT 10-plex (K, Protein N-term). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Nicotine increased 31 proteins (e.g., APP, APLP2, LAPTM4B, NCOA4) across all four cell lines; ~40% membrane/signaling; autophagy-related pathwaysNicotine treatment induced reproducible proteomic alterations across HEK293, HeLa, PaSC/RLT-PSC and SH-SY5Y cell lines; 8590 proteins were quantified, 31 proteins showed ≥1.5-fold increased abundance in all four cell lines, with enrichment of membrane/signaling proteins and autophagy-related candidates such as APP, APLP2, LAPTM4B and NCOA4.
Data_Caveats: Cell-line perturbation dataset, not a clinical tumor/normal cohort. Nicotine exposure was tested at a single dose and time point: 1 µM for 24 h. Quantification is relative TMT-based abundance, not absolute protein concentration. PaSC was included as duplicate/mock-nicotine pair, while the design is primarily cross-cell-line perturbation. Poor-quality PSMs, MS3 spectra with >8 missing TMT channels, summed reporter S/N <100, or no MS3 spectra were excluded.

Title: Isoelectric point-based fractionation by HiRIEF coupled to LC-MS allows for in-depth quantitative analysis of the phosphoproteome
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: HeLa human cervix adenocarcinoma cell line; Epithelial cell line; harvested in exponential growth phase
Experimental Design: TMT 10-plex non-phospho HiRIEF (pH 3–10), asynchronous untreated HeLa cell line
Short Description: Non-phospho HiRIEF LC-MS/MS TMT 10-plex dataset on asynchronous untreated HeLa cervix adenocarcinoma cells; from full 10-plex design only 4 untreated channels retained for atlas
Normalization Strategy: Protein-level TMT reporter-ion ratios to the average of four untreated HeLa control channels; median PSM ratios per gene with median channel normalization.
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT 10-plex (K, Protein N-term). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Standard HiRIEF LC-MS/TMT quantified 9,350 proteins corresponding to 9,182 genes in HeLa cells.
Data_Caveats: Atlas entry uses only the standard non-phospho protein-level proteome. The original TMT 10-plex design included untreated, pervanadate-treated, and mitotic-arrested HeLa samples, but only the four untreated asynchronous control channels are retained for atlas-level representation. Values are relative TMT ratios, not raw intensities or absolute abundances.
Quantification_Format: TMT protein ratios to untreated mean; median-normalized

Title: Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP/ACP5) promotes metastasis-related properties via TGFβ2/TβR and CD44 in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: MDA-MB-231 invasive breast cancer cell line; harvested at equal confluence
Disease Subtype: MDA-MB-231 TRAP-overexpressing breast cancer cell line; scrambled shRNA / TRAP shRNA knockdown
Experimental Design: Cell-line perturbation experiment: MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells with scrambled shRNA controls versus TRAP/ACP5 shRNA knockdown cells.
Short Description: TMT 10-plex proteome profiling of TRAP/ACP5-perturbed MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells. Four channels are scrambled shRNA controls, and six channels are TRAP/ACP5 knockdown samples using TRAP sh2 or TRAP sh3+4.
Normalization Strategy: Protein-level TMT 10-plex reporter-ion ratios were calculated relative to the average scrambled shRNA control group. Scrambled shRNA channels served as the reference/control for TRAP/ACP5 knockdown channels
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT 10-plex (K, Protein N-term). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: TRAP/ACP5 promotes metastasis-related properties in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, including proliferation, migration and invasion, partly through TGFβ2/TβR signaling and CD44-associated regulation.
Data_Caveats: In vitro breast cancer cell-line perturbation dataset, not patient tumor/normal material. The TMT subset contains TRAP-overexpressing MDA-MB-231 cells with 4 scrambled shRNA controls and 6 TRAP/ACP5 knockdown samples; healthy controls are absent.
Quantification_Format: Processed protein-level TMT reporter-ion intensities per channel

Title: Proteomics Profiling of CLL Versus Healthy B-cells Identifies Putative Therapeutic Targets and a Subtype-independent Signature of Spliceosome Dysregulation
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Isolated B-cells (B-cell material) from PBMCs of CLL patients and healthy donors
Disease Subtype: IGHV-mutated, IGHV-unmutated, Trisomy 12, NOTCH1-mutant, SF3B1-mutant, CD38+
Experimental Design: Case-control TMT 10-plex quantitative proteomics of primary CLL B-cells versus healthy donor B-cells, with two TMT batches and healthy donor B-cell bridging controls; no experimental perturbation, prior clinical treatment recorded as patient metadata.
Short Description: Case-control, TMT 10-plex, two-batch quantitative proteomics; primary CLL B-cells vs healthy donor B-cells; prior clinical treatment metadata available.
Normalization Strategy: Processed relative TMT protein quantification reported as log2(CLL/HDB) ratios. Protein-level values were derived from TMT reporter-ion intensities using SPIQuE-weighted PSM contributions and normalized to healthy donor B-cell bridging controls across two TMT 10-plex batches
Modifications: Fixed: Methylthio (C); TMT (K, Protein N-term). Variable: TMT (Y); Oxidation (M); Deamidation (N, Q); Phosphorylation (S, T, Y)
Main_Finding: TMT proteomics revealed a subtype-independent CLL protein-expression signature dominated by mRNA-processing/spliceosome dysregulation and highlighted candidate therapeutic and surface targets in primary CLL B-cells.
Data_Caveats: Initial cohort included 14 CLL samples and 3 healthy donor B-cell controls; final downstream analysis used 13 CLL samples and 3 controls after exclusion of CLL sample 4621 as an outlier. Healthy donor B-cells were reused across both TMT 10-plex batches as inter-batch bridging controls. The dataset is a small discovery-stage cohort with heterogeneous CLL molecular subtypes; subtype-specific comparisons have low statistical power. Values are processed relative log2(CLL/HDB) ratios, not raw TMT reporter intensities.
Quantification_Format: Processed relative TMT protein quantification reported as log2(CLL/HDB) ratios using healthy donor B-cell bridging controls

Title: Pilot Study on Mass Spectrometry Based Analysis of the Proteome of CD34+CD123+ Progenitor Cells for the Identification of Potential Targets for Immunotherapy in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: CD34+CD123+ hematopoietic/leukemic progenitor cells
Disease Subtype: FAB M4; sAML (from CMML); FAB M5; FAB M1
Experimental Design: Case-control TMT 10-plex proteomics of FACS-sorted CD34+CD123+ hematopoietic/leukemic progenitor cells, with separate cytosolic and membrane subcellular fractions.
Short Description: TMT 10-plex analysis of FACS-sorted CD34+CD123+ progenitor cells from 5 AML patients and 5 G-CSF–mobilized healthy donors, including cytosolic and membrane fractions.
Normalization Strategy: Median normalized; log2-transformed reporter ion intensities
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT6plex (K). Variable: TMT6plex (Protein N-term); Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: CD34+CD123+ AML progenitor cells showed altered cytosolic and membrane-associated proteomes compared with healthy G-CSF–mobilized donor progenitors, with affected Rho GTPase signaling, actin cytoskeleton organization, migration-related pathways, cytokine regulation, and metabolic processes
Data_Caveats: Small pilot cohort: 5 AML patients and 5 healthy donor controls. Healthy controls were G-CSF–mobilized stem cell donors, not steady-state healthy bone marrow controls. Cytosolic and membrane fractions were processed separately and should not be combined. CD123 was used for FACS sorting but was not detected in the proteomic dat
Quantification_Format: Median-normalized, log2-transformed TMT reporter ion intensities. AML/control log2 fold changes were calculated as the difference between mean AML and mean donor log2 abundances within each subcellular fraction

Title: Discovery of coding regions in the human genome by integrated proteogenomics analysis workflow
Tissue Cell Type Detailed:
5 normal tissues (placenta, liver, kidney, tonsil, testis)         
17 individual donors (all tissue samples from different individuals)
Organ: Multiple organs  Placenta, Liver, Kidney, Tonsil, Testis
Experimental Design: Deep TMT10plex HiRIEF LC-MS/MS proteomics of five histologically normal human tissues using the IPAW proteogenomics workflow to discover novel protein-coding regions

Title: Quantitative proteomics identifies conserved proteins and altered regulation of mucin-16 in low grade serous ovarian cancers
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: 12 FFPE LGSOC tumors; 24 FFPE HGSOC tumors; 12 benign FFPE fallopian tube tissues; laser microdissected tumor epithelium / whole tissue equivalents
Tissue: Ovarian serous carcinoma tissue; benign fallopian tube tissue
Tumor Type: Low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma; High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
Experimental Design: Case-control; discovery cohort + independent validation; multiplexed TMT11 proteomics
Short Description: Quantitative TMT11 LC-MS/MS proteomics of 48 FFPE tissues comparing LGSOC, HGSOC and benign fallopian tube to identify conserved subtype-specific proteins including MUC16.
TMT Channels Comparison: LGSOC vs HGSOC; LGSOC vs FT; HGSOC vs FT
TMT Additional Channels: Pooled internal reference (126) + partially unused channels across some plexes
Normalization Strategy: Reporter ion intensity-based protein normalization (not fully specified)
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl(C); TMT11plex(K); TMT11plex(N-term) Variable: Oxidation(M); Hydroxylation
Main_Finding: LGSOC and HGSOC have distinct proteomic signatures; 275 conserved differential proteins validated; LGSOC showed elevated MUC16/CD73 and adhesion-related programs, HGSOC cell-cycle programs.
Data_Caveats: Small discovery cohort; FFPE material; uneven TMT channel occupancy; normalization details incompletely described.
